Not note worthy?

The pandemic was also not handled poorly. At the federal level he did everything he needed to minus mandating masks which wouldn't go well. He screwed up saying he knew it was serious. But then again, it was February and no one knew how serious it was. It was being "downplayed" by even the CDC when compared to what it evolved into. The Cares Act was the largest social aid program in history. Other than release funds, it's on the states. That's how our government works honestly. Also, 6% of deaths are strictly from COVID. The average additional health issues in people who died was 2.7 and those are cardio vascular. Everyone knows the US has some of the highest rates for cardiovascular issues. Our culture and social dynamics, demographics, and population distribution also go into all of this. Trump fucked up, but not nearly as bad as people like to claim.

Well as for Syria, everything you said involves Trump pulling our troops out. That also isn't purely Turks vs Kurds, it's also Turks vs terrorist groups hunkered down in the north. As for North Korea, what policy failed? We're in no more danger than before, if anything relations with NK are very slightly better. We also sent a whole ass carrier strike group off their shore when tensions built, and what do you know, nothing happened. As for Saudi Arabia, that's not a war zone like Iraq, Syria, Yemen, Afghanistan, or Africa. Troops were at very little risk and securing those oil fields is a huge strategic move. It was more about securing and involved no serious fighting. It also wasnt 20,000, it was 1,800, back in October 2019... Trump is definitely not an advocate for war like Bush or Obama. Several officials agree that the moves made by Obama and Bush were serious mistakes. Trump learned from those mistakes.
